name: Projectile System
description: Owns everything between the trigger pull and the damage handoff: spawn, flight, and termination of projectiles. Hitscan is modelled as a projectile with infinite speed and zero travel time, so one code path serves both pistols and rockets — the difference is a tuning row, not a second system. Spread and recoil live here because they modify the shot at the instant of firing; deciding WHEN a shot may fire is combat.weapon_loadout's job, and deciding what a hit DOES is combat.damage_resolver's. This component never decrements ammo: it listens for combat.fireRequested and trusts that combat.ammo_economy has already counted the bullet, because two components counting the same resource is how magazines go negative. Ballistic drop reads movement.physics_core's gravity so a bullet and a thrown rock agree about the world.

inputs.name: projectileSpeed
inputs.description: Muzzle velocity in units per second. Values at or above 1000 are treated as hitscan — no simulated flight, just an immediate ray query. Kept as a number rather than a boolean flag so a 'fast bullet' and a 'laser' differ only in degree.

inputs.name: maxRange
inputs.description: Travel distance before the projectile expires unhit. Exists so missed shots terminate; without it every stray round simulates forever and the active count becomes a memory leak with recoil.

inputs.name: spreadDegrees
inputs.description: Base cone of random deviation per shot. Bloom from sustained fire or movement is layered on by combat.weapon_loadout via the fire request payload — this is the floor, not the ceiling.

inputs.name: recoilKick
inputs.description: Aim displacement applied to the shooter per shot, in degrees. Reported here because it is a property of the round being fired; recovering from recoil (return-to-center speed) belongs to whoever owns the camera or aim vector.

inputs.name: gravityScale
inputs.description: Multiplier on movement.physics_core's gravity for ballistic drop. 0 is a flat laser-like trajectory, 1 drops like a thrown object. Read per shot so tracer darts and grenades can coexist on one system.

inputs.name: collisionRadius
inputs.description: Thickness of the projectile for hit tests. 0 is a pure ray (hitscan feel); larger values let slow projectiles catch grazes, which reads as generosity rather than inaccuracy.

outputs.name: activeProjectileCount
outputs.description: Live simulated projectiles right now. Hitscan shots never appear here — they resolve in the same tick they are requested.

outputs.name: lastShotResolved
outputs.description: Whether the most recent fire request produced at least one hit. A convenience for feedback layers; the full hit list is on the event, not this output.
